nodes.summary: For an independent dominating set instance with $n$ vertices and edge list $E$, the graph of the instance is the simple graph on $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$ in which distinct vertices $u$ and $v$ are adjacent when $(u, v)$ or $(v, u)$ belongs to $E$.
nodes.title: Graph of an independent dominating set instance

nodes.summary: The decision problem INDEPENDENT DOMINATING SET accepts a bitstring $x$ exactly when $x$ decodes, under the canonical bitstring encoding, to an independent dominating set instance $(n, E, K)$ that is well formed and whose graph has an independent dominating set of at most $K$ vertices. It rejects every bitstring that does not decode to an instance.
nodes.title: INDEPENDENT DOMINATING SET as a decision problem

nodes.summary: An independent dominating set instance $(n, E, K)$ has a small independent dominating set when there is a set $S$ of vertices of its graph with at most $K$ elements such that every vertex lies in $S$ or is adjacent to a vertex of $S$, and no two distinct vertices of $S$ are adjacent.
nodes.title: Instances with a small independent dominating set

nodes.summary: An instance of INDEPENDENT DOMINATING SET is a triple $(n, E, K)$ of a natural number $n$, the number of vertices, a list $E$ of pairs of natural numbers, the edges, and a natural number $K$, the bound on the size of the set.
nodes.title: Independent dominating set instances

nodes.summary: The decision problem INDEPENDENT DOMINATING SET belongs to NP, and every decision problem in NP has a polynomial-time many-one reduction to it.
nodes.title: INDEPENDENT DOMINATING SET is NP-complete

nodes.summary: An independent dominating set instance $(n, E, K)$ is well formed when the list $E$ has no repeated entries and every pair $(a, b)$ in $E$ satisfies $a < n$, $b < n$, $a \ne b$, and $(b, a)$ does not belong to $E$.
nodes.title: Well-formed independent dominating set instances
